summary: Ikuhisa Takigawa studied at Waseda University and works in Indology and Buddhist studies. In 2002, he was attested as a part-time lecturer at both Waseda University and Tokai University.
Ikuko Tazaki is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2017, she was attested as a special researcher at Otani University and an affiliated researcher at Kyoto University.

Ikuro Hattori, holding a PhD from Pune University, works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He was attested as a researcher (2003) and full-time researcher (2026) at Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute, and a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (2026).

Ilkka Pyysiäinen is a religious studies scholar who studied under René Gothóni. He became an Academy Research Fellow at the University of Helsinki in 1984 and served as a visiting researcher at the University of Oxford.

Imran Philip works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Attested in 2026, he conducted doctoral studies under Kaustubh Mani Sengupta and held the Dr. Zakir Hussain Fellowship at The Asiatic Society.

Indologist and linguist Imre Bangha studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Visva-Bharati University, where he also worked (~1993–2000). Around 2003, he became Associate Professor of Hindi at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College; he is also an Honorary Professor at ELTE.

Imre Galambos specializes in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. After earning an MA at Eötvös Loránd University and a PhD at UC Berkeley, he held posts at the British Library, Cambridge, Hamburg, and Zhejiang University.

Imre Hamar studied at Eötvös Loránd University, National Taiwan Normal University, and under Noritoshi Aramaki. He became a professor at Eötvös Loránd University in 2006 and has served as a visiting professor at Otani University.

In-gun Kang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, Jesuit School of Theology, and Heythrop College under Michael Barnes, alongside teachers including Aloysius Pieris and Asanga Tilakaratne.

Ines Konczak-Nagel works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She has held posts at the Berlin State Museums, Ryukoku University (2012), and the University of Leipzig's Kuča-Projekt (attested 2026).
Ingmar Heise works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University by 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. After earning his PhD in 2000 at the Free University of Berlin, where he held a post attested in 2008, he became a professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 2018).
Inyoung Chung is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner (attested 2008).

Ioan Petru Culianu was a scholar of religious studies and history. He studied at the University of Bucharest, Catholic University of the Sacred Heart, Paris-Sorbonne, and under Mircea Eliade, later holding posts at Groningen (1976–1986) and Chicago (1986–1991).
Iona Macgregor specializes in Indology and linguistics. She studied and is attested in 2026 as a project researcher (Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin) at the University of Hamburg.
Ippei Okamoto works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held a post at Toyo University (attested 2014) and was attested as a visiting researcher at Minobusan University in 2026.

Irach Jehangir Sorabji Taraporewala worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He served as Professor of Iranian Studies at Deccan College (~1939–1942) and Vice-President of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1956).

Irawati Karve studied at Fergusson College and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. She served as Professor of Sociology and Anthropology at Deccan College (~1939–1970) and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1951–1952).

Irfan Habib is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University (~1947–1953) and New College (~1954–1958), and has held a post as a historian at Aligarh Muslim University since circa 1953.

Irving Babbitt was a philosopher who studied at Harvard College, the University of Paris, and Harvard University. He held academic posts at Williams College (~1893–1894) and Harvard University (~1894–1933).
